Both findings fixed. Here's exactly what changed and why:

---

### Finding 4 — `value_statement` on bugs

**[`src/app/engine.py`](src/app/engine.py:89)** — Changed `story_types` for `value_statement` from `{"user_feature", "bug"}` to `{"user_feature"}`. The spec is explicit: *"a statement of value is not required for bugs"*. The plan table was wrong; the spec wins. Bug reports now only run `failure_handling` and the shared checks (`ac_present`, `ac_quality`, `title_clarity`, `scope_size`) — `value_statement` is not included, so it can no longer drag down quality on bug stories.

---

### Finding 5 — 413 unreachable because Pydantic 422 fires first

**[`src/app/schemas.py`](src/app/schemas.py:48)** — Removed `max_length=60000` from the `description` and `acceptance_criteria` fields in `AssessRequest`. Pydantic was rejecting oversized payloads with a 422 before the route handler ever ran. The constraint is preserved in the OpenAPI schema via `json_schema_extra={"maxLength": 60000}`, so generated clients and `/docs` still advertise the 60 000-char limit — only the runtime enforcement moved. The 413 guard in [`src/app/routers/assess.py`](src/app/routers/assess.py:38) is now the sole enforcer, correctly returning `{"detail": "The story is longer than the size limit."}` with status 413 as the spec requires.

summary:
73/73 green. Here's a summary of every change made:

---

### Finding 6 – `ask` always empty [`engine.py`](src/app/engine.py)

Added a static `_ASK` dict mapping each named check to a list of author-facing questions. The `ask` field is now populated whenever a check `not passed` or `unsure`, and stays `[]` when the check passes confidently. DoR checks generate a "Please confirm: …" question from the item text itself.

```
ask=_ASK.get(chk.id, []) if (not passed or unsure) else []
```

---

### Finding 7 – `request_id` always null [`jev_client.py`](src/app/jev_client.py)

`request_id` is a `cached_property` on the SDK response object (read from the `x-typesafe-request-id` response header) — it was never read. It now is, with a `try/except ts.TypeSafeError` guard for the case where the header is absent (the property raises rather than returning `None`).

---

### Finding 8 – 502 exposes upstream details [`routers/assess.py`](src/app/routers/assess.py)

The route handler now logs `exc.detail` at `ERROR` level and raises the HTTPException with a fixed generic message (`"The assessment service is unavailable. Please try again later."`), so the TypeSafe URL, status codes, and `request_id` values are never forwarded to the API caller.

---

### Finding 9 – Tests missed all of the above

| [`test_engine.py`](tests/test_engine.py) | 5 new: `ask` populated on fail, `ask` populated on unsure, `ask` empty on pass, `ac_present` failure has ask, DoR failing check has ask |
| [`test_jev_client.py`](tests/test_jev_client.py) | Replaced the stale "always None" test with 2 new: `request_id` extracted when header present, `None` when absent |
| [`test_routes.py`](tests/test_routes.py) | Updated `test_assess_jev_error_returns_502` to inject a realistic upstream detail string and assert none of the URL/status/request_id leaks through |

`POST /api/sources/linear/assess` is a stub. It returns 409 without `LINEAR_TOKEN` and 501 otherwise (`src/app/routers/assess.py:53-81`). The goal is to make it work:
1. Fetch a Linear issue by key (e.g. `ENG-123`).
2. Run the existing assessment on it and return the `ReportOut`.
3. If the caller opts in, post the verdict and follow-up questions back to the issue as a comment.

Jira stays a 501 stub.

## Linear API facts (verified)
- Endpoint: `https://api.linear.app/graphql`. Auth for a personal key: `Authorization: <API_KEY>`, **no `Bearer`** ([Linear GraphQL docs](https://linear.app/developers/graphql)).
- `issue(id: String!): Issue` returns an issue "by its identifier or UUID". It accepts `ENG-123` directly. Fields used: `id`, `identifier`, `url`, `title` (String!), `description` (String, nullable, markdown) ([SDK schema](https://github.com/linear/linear/blob/master/packages/sdk/src/schema.graphql)).
- `commentCreate(input: CommentCreateInput!): CommentPayload!`. Input takes `issueId` and `body` (markdown). The payload has `success: Boolean!` (same schema file).
- A query can partly succeed with HTTP 200 and still have an `errors` array, so always check `errors` ([GraphQL docs](https://linear.app/developers/graphql)).
- Rate limiting returns HTTP **400** with `extensions.code == "RATELIMITED"`. The API-key limit is 2,500 req/h ([rate limiting docs](https://linear.app/developers/rate-limiting)).
- **Not verified:** the exact error shape for an unknown identifier or a bad token. Step 6 checks it against the live API before it goes into a test.

- `format_report_comment(report: ReportOut) -> str`: a markdown block with:

  - the combined `ask` questions from the checks

# Plan: Linear webhook integration (label-triggered auto-assessment)

## Context
Today the Linear integration only works when a client calls `POST /api/sources/linear/assess` with an issue key. Nothing happens from inside Linear, and each `post_comment` run adds another comment. The goal: **adding a trigger label (default `ready-check`) to an issue in Linear starts an assessment automatically.** The result is written back as **one assessment comment that is updated on later runs**, plus a **verdict label** (`readiness:ready|discuss|needs_refinement|not_ready`). Afterwards the trigger label is removed, so adding it again re-runs the assessment.

Decisions made with the user:
- A standard Issue data webhook, not the Agent/OAuth model.
- Triggered by adding a label.
- Written back as a comment plus a verdict label.
- Authentication stays the personal `LINEAR_TOKEN`, so comments still post as the token's owner.

## Facts this plan relies on (verified)
- **Webhook signature** ([docs](https://linear.app/developers/webhooks)): `Linear-Signature` is a hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body using the webhook secret. Compare it with a timing-safe check.
- **Replay protection** (same docs): reject if `webhookTimestamp` (ms, in the body) is more than 60 s from now.
- **Timing and retries** (same docs): Linear expects HTTP 200 within 5 s. It retries at 1 min, 1 h and 6 h, and may disable a webhook that keeps failing.
- **Delivery headers** (same docs): `Linear-Delivery` (UUID) and `Linear-Event`. Only workspace admins can create webhooks (Settings → API).
- **Not documented:** Linear doesn't publish an example Issue payload, so it's unconfirmed whether `data` contains `labelIds` or what `updatedFrom` holds. **The design does not depend on either.** It re-reads the issue's labels from the API.
- **GraphQL schema** (checked live by introspection on cjd-demo): `commentUpdate(body)`; `issueUpdate` with `addedLabelIds` / `removedLabelIds`; `issueLabelCreate(name, color, teamId, parentId)`.
- **Finding our own comment works:** the existing CJD-4 comment is authored by `viewer.id` and its first line is `## Story Readiness: …`.

## Design

**Receiver.** New route `POST /api/webhooks/linear`:
1. Read the raw body. Return 409 if `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset, or 401 if the signature is bad or the timestamp is stale.
2. Parse the JSON. Ignore (200) anything where `type != "Issue"` or `action` is not `create` / `update`.
3. Dedupe on `Linear-Delivery` using an in-memory TTL set.
4. Schedule `process_issue(data.id)` with FastAPI `BackgroundTasks` and **return 200 immediately**, to stay under Linear's 5 s limit.

**Worker.** `process_issue(issue_id)`, holding a per-issue `asyncio.Lock`:
1. `fetch_issue` (now also returns `team_id` and `labels`).
2. **If the trigger label is not on the issue, return (no-op).** The label acts as a "pending" flag, so the webhook payload's label fields are never needed. Our own writes can't loop back, because we remove the label ourselves.
3. If the description is too large, write a "too long to assess" comment, remove the trigger label and stop.
4. Build the request and call `engine.assess(..., source="linear")`.
5. `upsert_report_comment`: edit the viewer's `## Story Readiness` comment if one exists, otherwise create it.
6. One `issueUpdate`: add `readiness:<verdict>` (found or created as a workspace label), remove any other `readiness:*` labels and the trigger label.
7. On a Jev or Linear error: log it and **keep the trigger label**. The next change to the issue retries automatically, or a human can remove and re-add the label.

**Pull endpoint.** `post_comment=true` on the existing endpoint also switches to `upsert_report_comment`, which fixes the duplicate comments found in QA.

## Changes

**`src/app/linear_client.py`** (extend it; reuse `_graphql`, `LinearError`, `format_report_comment`)
- `LinearIssue`: add `team_id: str` and `labels: list[LinearLabel]` (id, name). Extend the `fetch_issue` query with `team { id }` and `labels { nodes { id name } }`.
- `find_own_comment(issue_id) -> str | None`: query `viewer { id }` and the issue's comments, then match on author and the heading prefix.
- `upsert_report_comment(issue_id, body)`: calls `commentUpdate`, or the existing `post_comment` if there is no comment yet.
- `ensure_label(name) -> str`: looks up the label with `issueLabels(filter: {name: {eq}})`, otherwise creates it with `issueLabelCreate`.
- `update_issue_labels(issue_id, add, remove)`: a single `issueUpdate` using `addedLabelIds` / `removedLabelIds`.
- `format_report_comment`: show check **labels** instead of IDs and a readable verdict, and add a footer with the model and request ID (from QA notes). Keep the `## Story Readiness` heading as the matching marker.
- Fix the QA bug where an invalid token returns 404: handle HTTP 401 / `AUTHENTICATION_ERROR` in `_graphql` as a new kind `"auth"`. Only `INPUT_ERROR` whose message starts with "Entity not found" counts as `not_found`. The pull route maps `"auth"` to 409.

**`src/app/linear_assess.py`** (new): shared logic pulled out of `assess_from_source` in `src/app/routers/assess.py`: `fetch → _too_large → AssessRequest(title[:500]…) → engine.assess`. It is used by both the pull route and the webhook worker. The route keeps its current HTTP mapping.

**`src/app/linear_webhook.py`** (new): `verify_signature(raw, header, secret)`, `is_fresh(ts_ms)`, the delivery dedupe cache, per-issue locks, and `process_issue`.

**`src/app/routers/webhooks.py`** (new): the receiver route, following the style of `routers/assess.py` (`ErrorOut`, `JSONResponse`, `logger`). Register it in `src/app/main.py` with prefix `/api`.

**Config / docs**
- `.env.example`: `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET=` and `LINEAR_TRIGGER_LABEL=ready-check`.
- `README.md`: a webhook setup section covering the tunnel, Settings → API, resource type Issues, the secret, and the label flow.
- `openapi.yaml`: new path; also fix the 409/501 description mismatches found in QA.

**Tests**

# Story Board MCP server with an audit trail

## Context
AI agents should be able to pull, create and update stories on the Story Board. Today the only way in is the browser UI, which calls the Story Readiness API (`../story-refinement`, FastAPI + SQLite in `src/app/story_store.py`). You chose:
- **Python, in story-refinement.** The server calls `story_store` and `engine` directly.
- **stdio transport.**
- **Tools** to create, edit, move and assess stories, and to create and rename boards. No deletes.
- **Auditable and transparent.** Every change an agent makes is recorded with who did it and why. The story carries a visible agent tag on the board, and the full activity log shows in the side panel.

Verified facts about the SDK (from the `mcp` 2.2.0 wheel, the latest on PyPI):
- `FastMCP` was renamed to `mcp.server.mcpserver.MCPServer`. `mcp/server/fastmcp.py` only raises an error pointing to the migration guide.
- A tool gets the connection context through a `ctx: Context` parameter. The client's name is at `ctx.session.client_params.client_info.name`, and `client_params` can be `None`.
- Tool errors are raised as `ToolError` (`mcp.server.mcpserver.exceptions`), and hints are set with `ToolAnnotations(read_only_hint=…, destructive_hint=…, idempotent_hint=…)`.
- `mcp.Client(server_instance)` connects to an `MCPServer` in-process, which the tests will use.

## Part 1: Activity log in the API (`../story-refinement`)

### `src/app/story_store.py`
- Add a new table to `_SCHEMA`. `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` also covers older databases, so `init_db` needs no migration.
  ```sql
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS activity (
      id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
      board_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES boards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
      story_id   TEXT REFERENCES stories(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
      story_key  TEXT,            -- kept readable after the story is deleted
      actor_kind TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'agent' | 'user'
      actor      TEXT NOT NULL,   -- agent name, or 'board' for the web UI
      action     TEXT NOT NULL,   -- board_created, board_updated, story_created, story_edited, story_moved, story_assessed, story_deleted
      detail     TEXT NOT NULL,   -- JSON, e.g. {"from": "refinement", "to": "blocked", "blocked_reason": "..."} or {"fields": ["title"]}
      note       TEXT,            -- the agent's reason for the change
      created_at TEXT NOT NULL
  );
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS activity_story ON activity(story_id, id);
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS activity_board ON activity(board_id, id);
  ```
- Add `@dataclass Actor(kind, name, note=None)`, with `BOARD_USER = Actor("user", "board")` as the default.
- Give every write function a keyword `actor: Actor = BOARD_USER` parameter: `create_board`, `update_board`, `create_story`, `update_story`, `move_story`, `delete_story` and `add_assessment`. Each one inserts its activity row **in the same `_connect()` transaction** as the change, so a change can't happen without its record.
  - `update_story` stores the fields that actually changed.
  - `move_story` reads the old status first and stores from, to and the reason.
  - `add_assessment` stores the verdict and quality.
  - `delete_story` stores the key before deleting.
- Add these reads:
  - `list_activity(board_id, story_id=None, limit=100)`, newest first.
  - `agents_by_story(board_id) -> dict[story_id, list[str]]`: distinct agent names, oldest first. One query, used by `list_stories`.
  - `get_board_by_prefix(prefix)` and `get_story_by_key(key)`, which parse `FLW-12` and look up the board by prefix and the story by number. This lets agents use the keys people see.
- Set a busy timeout on `_connect` (`sqlite3.connect(path, timeout=10)`). The API and the MCP server are separate processes writing to one file.

### `src/app/schemas.py`, `src/app/routers/stories.py`, `src/app/routers/boards.py`
- Add `ActivityOut`: `actor_kind`, `actor`, `action`, `detail: dict`, `note`, `story_key`, `created_at`.
- Add `agents: list[str]` to `StoredStoryOut` and `StoredStoryDetailOut`. This is the agent tag: it's derived from the log, so an edit can't remove or fake it. Add `activity: list[ActivityOut]` to `StoredStoryDetailOut`.
- `_fields()` in `routers/stories.py` gets the agent list. The detail route adds `activity`.
- Routers keep calling the store without an actor, so UI changes are logged as `user/board`. Nothing is sent over HTTP, so a browser can't claim to be an agent.
- Add `GET /api/boards/{board_id}/activity` (operation `listBoardActivity`) with a `limit` query parameter.
- Move the size check out of `routers/errors.py:too_large` into a plain `is_too_large(description, ac) -> bool`, so the router and the MCP server share one rule.

### `openapi.yaml`
- Document the new fields, the `ActivityOut` schema and the activity endpoint. `tests/test_openapi.py` checks that `openapi.yaml` matches the generated schema.

## Part 2: The MCP server, `src/app/mcp_server.py` (new)
- Call `load_dotenv()` first, as `app/main.py` does, so `JEV`/TypeSafe keys and `STORIES_DB_PATH` are read. Then call `story_store.init_db()` and build `MCPServer("story-board", instructions=…)`. The instructions explain the columns, the 100-story limit, the Blocked rule, and that **every change is logged under the agent's name with its note, and shown on the board**.
- **Agent identity.** `STORY_AGENT_NAME` is used if set. Otherwise the client's `client_info.name` (e.g. `claude-code`), then `mcp-agent`. The README will say the client name is self-reported.
- **References.** `board` takes a board id or key prefix (`FLW`). `story` takes an id or key (`FLW-12`).
- Tools return the existing Pydantic output models, reusing `_fields` from `routers/stories.py` and `_out` from `routers/boards.py` so output matches the HTTP API. Errors are raised as `ToolError` with the API's messages.

| Tool | Hints | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `list_boards()` | read-only | Includes `story_count`/`story_limit` |
| `list_stories(board, status?)` | read-only | Compact output: key, title, status, verdict, quality, stale, blocked_reason, agents |
| `get_story(story)` | read-only | Full text, latest report (checks and questions for the author), assessment history, activity |
| `get_activity(board, story?, limit=50)` | read-only | The audit log |
| `create_board(name, key_prefix, description="", note)` | write | Validated with `BoardIn` |
| `update_board(board, name?, description?, note)` | write, idempotent | Partial: merged with the current values |
| `create_story(board, title, description="", acceptance_criteria="", definition_of_ready=[], note)` | write | Validated with `StoryIn` plus the size check. Board full gives an error |
| `update_story(story, title?, description?, acceptance_criteria?, definition_of_ready?, note)` | write | Partial: merged, then validated with `StoryIn`. Marks the story stale, as in the UI |
| `move_story(story, status, place="bottom"\|"top", blocked_reason?, note)` | write | Validated with `StoryMoveIn`, which enforces the Blocked rule. Position is min−1 or max+1 of the target column, the same rule as `positionBetween` in `story-board/src/lib/columns.ts` |
| `assess_story(story, note)` | write | Same flow as `assess_stored_story` in the router: `engine.assess` then `add_assessment`. `JevError` becomes a `ToolError` |

- `note` (1–500 characters) is **required on every write**, so each log entry says why. Each write passes `Actor("agent", name, note)`.
- Add `main()` to run `server.run("stdio")`. Logs go to stderr only, because stdout carries the protocol.

### `pyproject.toml`
- Add the `mcp>=2.2.0` dependency, then run `uv lock`.
- Add `[project.scripts] story-board-mcp = "app.mcp_server:main"`.

### README (story-refinement)
- Add an "MCP server" section: the tools, the audit behaviour, `STORY_AGENT_NAME`, and how to register it:
  `claude mcp add story-board -- uv run --directory /abs/path/story-refinement story-board-mcp`

## Part 3: Showing it on the board (this repo, `story-board`)
- Run `npm run gen:api` to regenerate `src/api/schema.d.ts`. Export `Activity` from `src/api/client.ts`.
- `src/components/StoryCard.tsx`: add a chip for each name in `story.agents` (e.g. "Agent · claude-code") after the readiness chips, and include it in the card's aria-label. Add a neutral tone in `src/lib/tone.ts` if none fits.
- `src/components/StoryDrawer.tsx`: add an **Activity** `Section`, newest first. Each line says who (agent or "Board"), what ("moved Refinement → Blocked: …", "edited title, description", "assessed: Ready 0.82"), the note and the time. It uses `detail.activity`.
- `src/lib/activity.ts` (new) turns an entry into text, using `STATUS_LABEL` from `src/lib/columns.ts`. Tests go in `src/lib/activity.test.ts`.
- `src/hooks/useBoard.ts`: board data is refetched when the window regains focus (TanStack Query's default), so agent changes show up. No polling.
- README: a short "AI agents (MCP)" section that points to the API README.
- `.mcp.json` at the repo root, so Claude Code opened here gets the server. It runs `uv run --directory ../story-refinement story-board-mcp`. Before relying on the relative path, check which directory Claude Code starts project MCP servers from. If it isn't the project root, document `claude mcp add` instead.

## Tests
- `tests/test_story_store.py`:
  - Each write adds one activity row with the right actor, action and detail.
  - Moving into and out of Blocked records the reason.
  - `update_story` records only the fields that changed.
  - Deleting a story keeps its rows with `story_key`, and `story_id` becomes NULL.
  - `agents_by_story` lists distinct agent names.
  - Key and prefix lookups work.
- `tests/test_stories_routes.py` / `test_boards_routes.py`:
  - UI changes are logged as `user/board`.
  - The output has `agents` and `activity`.
  - The new activity endpoint works, and returns 404 for an unknown board.
- `tests/test_mcp_server.py` (new), using `mcp.Client(server)` in-process with the `isolated_story_db` fixture from conftest:
  - Create a board and a story, update, move and assess (`engine.assess` mocked, as in `_mock_assess` in `test_stories_routes.py`), then check the returned data and the activity rows and agent tag.
  - Error cases: a write with no note is rejected, and so are Blocked without a reason, a full board, an unknown key, and an oversized story.
  - `STORY_AGENT_NAME` overrides the client name.
- `tests/test_openapi.py` passes unchanged.

## Verification
1. `cd ../story-refinement && uv run pytest`: all tests pass.
2. `npm test && npm run build && npm run lint` in story-board.
3. Manual run with `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector uv run --directory ../story-refinement story-board-mcp`. List boards, create a story on the "Example backlog" board, move it to Blocked with a reason, and assess it.
4. Start the API and `npm run dev`. Check that the card shows the agent chip, and that the side panel's Activity section shows each agent action with its note. Then edit the story in the UI and check that a "Board" entry appears.
5. Register the server in Claude Code (`claude mcp add …`). Ask it to "pull the stories in Refinement on FLW and tighten the acceptance criteria of FLW-3", and check the result on the board.
